info.title: klarfakt — validate EN 16931 electronic invoices
info.description: Command line validator for EN 16931 electronic invoices (UBL, CII, Factur-X).

options.name: --rules
options.description: en16931 | peppol | xrechnung (default: taken from the invoice)

options.name: --recursive
options.description: descend into subfolders, -r for short

options.name: --csv
options.description: write one row per invoice, with a summary on the console

options.name: --json
options.description: machine-readable output

options.name: --no-schema
options.description: check business rules only, skipping XML Schema

options.name: --strict
options.description:
fail an invoice whose declared specification has no rule set
here, instead of judging it against EN 16931 alone

options.name: --parallel
options.description: files validated at once (default: one per core)

options.name: --out
options.description: where to write rendered HTML; stdout for a single invoice

options.name: --lang
options.description:
label language for render: de (default) or en
Options apply to the command that reads them; anything else is refused rather
than ignored. "klarfakt <command> --help" lists what a command takes.
render produces a self-contained HTML page using the official XRechnung
visualisation, so what you show a user matches the reference rendering.
Run "rules restore" once: it downloads the validation artefacts from their
publishers and checks them against the SHA-256 recorded in the manifest.
Nothing else in Klarfakt touches the network.
Files may be UBL or CII XML, or a hybrid Factur-X / ZUGFeRD 2.x PDF. Point it at a
folder to see how much of an existing archive would be rejected.
Exit codes:
0   valid
1   validation errors
2   a file could not be processed
64  usage error
130 stopped with Ctrl+C before every file was checked
